My plan is to use the initial rounds for strategic exploration to model my opponents' behavior.

1.  **Establish a Baseline:** I will start by bidding the theoretically optimal amount for three rational bidders: 2/3 of my value. This will serve as a control group for my experiments.

2.  **Aggressive Probing:** I will test an aggressive strategy by bidding ~85% of my value, especially on mid-to-high values. This aims to secure wins to gather data on my opponents' bidding ranges and test if they are bidding timidly.

After these initial rounds, I will analyze their patterns and adapt my strategy to exploit any predictable behavior.

My plan is to start with a theoretically sound strategy and adapt based on my opponents' behavior.

**Phase 1: Exploration (Rounds 1-3)**
I will begin by bidding the Nash Equilibrium strategy: approximately 67% of my value. This provides a solid baseline. To gather data, I will test one more aggressive bid (~80% of my value) and one more conservative bid (~50%) to quickly learn if my opponents are over- or under-bidding.

**Phase 2: Adaptation (Rounds 4-10)**
I will analyze the bidding history to model my opponents. If they bid passively, I will lower my bids to increase my profit margin. If they are aggressive, I will bid more competitively, especially on high-value items, to secure profitable wins.

My plan is to systematically probe my opponents' strategies by varying my bid-to-value ratio across the initial rounds.

1.  **Baseline:** I'll begin by bidding the theoretical optimum, approximately 2/3 of my value. This establishes a benchmark for rational play.
2.  **Aggressive Probe:** Next, I will bid more aggressively, around 85% of my value. This tests my opponents' upper bidding limits and helps me win auctions to gather data, even at a lower profit margin.
3.  **Conservative Probe:** I will then bid conservatively, around 50% of my value, to see if I can secure wins with high profit margins.

Based on these results, I will model my opponents and adapt my strategy to bid just enough to win.

My analysis showed my baseline 2/3 bid was too conservative. For the next rounds, I'll adopt a tiered strategy. For high values (>$65), I'll bid an aggressive 80% to secure wins. For lower values, I'll bid a more moderate 60-70% to gather data without overpaying.

My analysis showed I overbid. This round, I'll test a more conservative strategy, bidding around 60% of my value. This is a deliberate deviation from the 67% Nash Equilibrium to test if I can increase my profit margin while still beating my opponents' likely bids.

My overarching plan remains to probe opponent strategies. This round, I will execute the first phase: a baseline probe. I will bid the theoretical optimum, which is two-thirds (2/3) of my private value. This will establish a rational benchmark and help me begin modeling my opponents' bidding behavior.

My Round 1 bid was far too high given my opponents' passivity. I will now test a much more conservative strategy to avoid overpaying. My new plan is to bid approximately 50-60% of my value. This is a data-gathering move to find the minimum winning bid and maximize profit.

My conservative strategy test is complete. For the next round, I will test a more aggressive approach. My plan is to bid 75% of my value. This will help me understand if a higher win-rate, even with a smaller profit margin, is a better long-term strategy against my opponents.

My 2/3 value strategy was too conservative against an aggressive opponent. To counter this, I will test a more aggressive strategy. This round, I will bid 85% of my private value. This will test the upper bound of profitable bidding and see how opponents react to a higher bid.

My previous strategies were too rigid and extreme. I will now test a value-dependent strategy. For high values (>$70), I will bid aggressively, around 75% of my value, to secure the win. For mid-range values, I'll bid more cautiously (~60%) to avoid overpaying and maximize my margin.

My plan is to test a classic auction theory strategy: bidding (N-1)/N of my value. With 3 total bidders, this translates to bidding approximately 2/3 (or 67%) of my value. This is a more conservative approach than last round, aimed at increasing my profit margin on wins.

My next strategy will be adaptive, based on my value. For high values (>$70), I will bid a safer 75% to secure a larger profit margin. For mid-range values ($40-$70), I will bid a more aggressive 85% to compete. For low values (<$40), I'll bid low.

The winner in round 3 bid ~2/3 of their value, a theoretically optimal strategy. I will test this model directly. My new plan is to bid exactly 2/3 of my own value, rounded to the nearest dollar. This will test its effectiveness and gather data on my opponents' rationality.

My opponents bid very conservatively last round. To capitalize on this and increase my profit margin, I will test a riskier strategy. I will bid a lower fraction of my value, specifically 50%. This should dramatically increase my profit if I win, which is my main goal.

My previous tiered-percentage plan is a good start, but I need more data. I'll test a simpler, theoretically-grounded strategy: bidding two-thirds (67%) of my value, regardless of the value. This aligns with the last winner's bid (42/63 ≈ 67%) and provides a consistent baseline for comparison.

My opponents appear rational, often bidding near the optimal 2/3 of their value. To exploit potentially timid bidding from them, I will test a more aggressive strategy. I will bid 75% of my value, aiming to capture more wins and see if a higher win-rate increases total profit.

My 50% bid was far too conservative, costing me a profitable win against an aggressive bidder. I must adapt. This round, I will test a more competitive strategy by bidding a higher fraction of my value, approximately 70%, to increase my chances of winning when I have a high value.

My last bid was a significant overpayment, revealing opponent conservatism. To maximize profit, I must bid lower. This round, I will test a simple, reduced strategy: bidding 50% of my value. This should increase my profit margin on any potential win and gather crucial data.
